title: Real Estate Broker Commission in India: Slabs, RERA Rules & Builder Payouts

faqs.question: How much commission does a real estate broker charge in India?
faqs.answer: On secondary market resale deals, brokers typically charge 1% to 2% of the transaction value from both the buyer and the seller. On residential rental deals, the fee is usually 15 days to 1 month's rent. For new project launches, channel partners charge buyers 0% and receive 2% to 5% directly from the builder.

faqs.question: Who pays the broker commission on new launch builder flats?
faqs.answer: In primary sales (new project launches), the builder or developer pays 100% of the commission to the channel partner or broker. The homebuyer pays zero brokerage fees.

faqs.question: Is real estate broker commission regulated by RERA?
faqs.answer: RERA does not cap or fix brokerage percentages; commission rates are governed by mutual agreement. However, RERA Section 9 mandates that brokers must be officially registered with the state RERA authority to legally facilitate sales and receive commissions on registered projects.

faqs.question: Is GST applicable on real estate brokerage in India?
faqs.answer: Yes. Brokerage services attract 18% Goods and Services Tax (GST). If the broker is GST-registered, they invoice the fee plus 18% GST. For corporate developer payouts, Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) under Section 194H also applies.

faqs.question: What is a 70/30 commission split in real estate?
faqs.answer: In real estate brokerage agencies, a 70/30 split means the individual agent keeps 70% of the gross commission earned on a deal, while the brokerage firm or principal channel partner retains 30% to cover office infrastructure, CRM software, marketing leads, and administrative support.

faqs.question: When does a builder pay commission to a channel partner?
faqs.answer: Builder commission payouts are tied to payment milestones. Typically, 50% of the commission is released when the buyer executes the Builder-Buyer Agreement (BBA) and pays the initial 10% to 20%, with the remaining balance disbursed upon milestone collection.

faqs.question: Can a homebuyer negotiate brokerage fees in India?
faqs.answer: Yes. In resale transactions, brokerage fees are negotiable. On high-ticket luxury transactions (above ₹2–3 Crore), buyers and sellers frequently negotiate the rate down from 2% to 1% or agree on a flat lump-sum fee.

faqs.question: Should builders rely only on broker networks or their own digital ads?
faqs.answer: Relying solely on broker networks costs developers 3% to 5% per unit plus kicker bonuses. Leading developers run a hybrid model: maintaining strong channel partner relationships while running their own digital lead engine (Meta ads, project landing pages, and instant WhatsApp response) where customer acquisition costs are often under 1.5%.
